RaMP multi-database ORA reported KEGG:map00350 as rank-7 among 15 pathways (FDR = 3.72 × 10⁻⁴; fold-enrichment = 261; hit metabolites: 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde and catechol, both also anchoring seven SMPDB disease pathways — Alkaptonuria, Dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency, Hawkinsinuria, and others — all sharing the same FDR). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00350 entry at rank-5 with p = 0.148 (single-metabolite hit of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde on a 42-member pathway). The cross-paradigm consensus was reinforced by a secondary KEGG hit: **Biopterin metabolism** (MUMM rank 2, p = 0.065), directly linking 7,8-dihydrobiopterin (the tetrahydrobiopterin cofactor required by phenylalanine/tyrosine hydroxylases) to the aromatic-amino-acid catabolic axis. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on a single biological domain as the dominant signal: **Tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:map00350)**. RaMP multi-database ORA reported KEGG:map00350 as rank-7 among 15 pathways (FDR = 3.72 × 10⁻⁴; fold-enrichment = 261; hit metabolites: 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde and catechol, both also anchoring seven SMPDB disease pathways — Alkaptonuria, Dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency, Hawkinsinuria, and others — all sharing the same FDR). Mummichog m/z-direct scoring placed 'Tyrosine metabolism' first with a permutation p-value of 0.0034 and an exceptional 11/11 input-mapped hits on the mummichog network (7,8-dihydrobiopterin, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, 5,6-dihydroxyindole, and eight structurally adjacent analogues). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00350 entry at rank-5 with p = 0.148 (single-metabolite hit of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde on a 42-member pathway). The cross-paradigm consensus was reinforced by a secondary KEGG hit: **Biopterin metabolism** (MUMM rank 2, p = 0.065), directly linking 7,8-dihydrobiopterin (the tetrahydrobiopterin cofactor required by phenylalanine/tyrosine hydroxylases) to the aromatic-amino-acid catabolic axis. Human1 pathway-membership queries verified that 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (CHEBI:27978), 5,6-dihydroxyindole (CHEBI:27404), and catechol (CHEBI:18135) are all canonical members of HUMAN1:tyrosine_metabolism, while 7,8-dihydrobiopterin (CHEBI:64277) is a canonical member of HUMAN1:biopterin_metabolism; 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (CHEBI:371) is further confirmed as a HUMAN1 member linking tyrosine metabolism to proline/arginine catabolism. Eicosapentaenoic acid (all-cis-5,8,11,14,17-icosapentaenoic acid, KEGG:C06428) appeared independently in GPCR-signalling Reactome pathways (R-HSA-388396, R-HSA-500792) and in fatty-acid metabolism networks, consistent with its known anti-inflammatory EPA activity, but its signal is secondary to the robust tyrosine/metabolism core. The biological story centres on perturbation of the tyrosine catabolic scaffold: a dihydrobiopterin cofactor deficiency would impair phenylalanine hydroxylase activity, upstream of the tyrosine-to-L-DOPA-to-dopamine-to-norepinephrine cascade; the resulting accumulation or differential abundance of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde and catechol — both highly reactive catecholaldehyde/catechol intermediates — drives the enriched disease-module signatures across four independent enrichment methods.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on perturbation of tyrosine metabolism and its linked biopterin cofactor network. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00350 (Tyrosine metabolism) as rank-7 among 15 pathways with FDR = 3.72 × 10⁻⁴, driven by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C04043) and catechol (KEGG:C15571). Mummichog m/z-direct activity reported the same network as its top hit (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, p = 0.00387) with all 11 input compounds mapped, including dihydrobiopterin (KEGG:C02953), 5,6-dihydroxyindole (KEGG:C05578), and the two driver metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00350 at rank-5 (p = 0.148) with a single input hit for 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde. Three driver metabolites — dihydrobiopterin, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, and 5,6-dihydroxyindole — mapped across both primary pathway hits, anchoring the cross-paradigm signal.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on perturbation of tyrosine metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00350 (Tyrosine metabolism) as rank-7 among 15 pathways with FDR = 3.72 × 10⁻⁴, driven by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde and catechol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00350 at rank-5 with p-value = 0.148, with 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde as the sole mapped input. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism as the top hit (p = 0.00176) and mapped all 11 input compounds including dihydrobiopterin, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, and 5,6-dihydroxyindole. The two driver metabolites are 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde and catechol; both are confirmed members of the tyrosine metabolism scaffold across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms.
